source_text.body:
Turn lesson notes into tailored student feedback documents
A language teacher uses an AI agent to turn notes into a formatted feedback document with corrections, explanations and homework tailored to each student's errors.
·
Oct 23, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The teacher writes rough class notes in Notion during lessons—errors heard, what was covered, and what to do next—then has AI turn those notes overnight into a formatted student feedback document with corrections, explanations, error-pattern summaries, and homework matched to those patterns. The system also updates a running file for each student, and at week’s end reviews accumulated feedback and notes to draft upcoming lessons; the teacher reviews, fixes, and sends everything.
How it went
Feedback time dropped from about 30 minutes per student to roughly 2–5 minutes, and the teacher says the documents and lesson materials are better and deeper than before. It still needs human review, can produce too much detail, and works only as well as the notes and rules behind it.
Worth knowing
The hardest part was writing and continually tweaking the rules so the feedback sounded like the teacher rather than a chatbot.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I teach [language] to [level] students. Here are my lesson notes for [student name]: [paste notes with their errors and topics covered]. Write a formatted feedback document with their corrections, a short clear explanation of each mistake, and 5 to 8 homework exercises targeting those specific errors. Keep the tone [encouraging/direct], and finish with the document ready to copy into [Google Docs/Word].
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/edtech/comments/1wvi9su/ive_been_teaching_adults_in_korea_for_16_years
